quotes.text: Every AI system gets ranked into one of four categories unacceptable, high, limited, or minimal. That box isn't cosmetic. It dictates the exact compliance weights strapped to you
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the AI Act's four risk tiers and why the classification matters.

quotes.text: But classification isn't about what the system looks like. It's about what it does and in what context you use it. Minimal doesn't mean permanent free pass.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the key point that use and context, not the tool, determine risk class.

quotes.text: Copilot doesn't erase your duties. The act enforces a shared responsibility model. Microsoft delivers the scaffolding. You still must configure log and operate within it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that deployers keep their obligations even with a compliant-by-design tool.

quotes.text: Regulators don't question whether Microsoft Purview exists. They ask if you implemented the controls. They won't accept Copilot has logging options. They'll demand your logs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pithy reminder that compliance means proof of configured controls, not owning tools.

quotes.text: Rules don't kill technology, they make it usable at scale. The assumption that regulation equals stagnation is as flawed as thinking speed limits killed the automobile.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable argument that regulation enables rather than blocks AI adoption.

takeaways: Under the EU AI Act, a system's risk class depends on how and where you use it, so the same generative tool can move from limited to high risk.
Copilot inherits Microsoft 365 governance such as tenant boundaries, Purview and audit logs, while standalone ChatGPT leaves deployers to build those safeguards themselves.
Deployers still need a DPIA and processing records, data classification and DLP, retained audit logs and role-based AI literacy training.
hook: Think AI compliance is Microsoft's or OpenAI's problem? Under the EU AI Act, deployers share the obligations. This episode helps IT, compliance and data protection leads compare Copilot and ChatGPT, understand the risk ladder and set up the checklist auditors will actually ask for.
